newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam slashes interest rates to bolster economy.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam slashes interest rates to bolster economy.

text.p: Vietnam's central bank on Tuesday lowered interest rates for the fourth time this year in a bid to keep economic growth on a fast track.

The State Bank of Vietnam said that, with immediate effect, the interest rate ceiling on short-term local currency loans was cut to 1.25 percent per month from 1.50 percent. The limit on such loans began the year at 2.1 percent.
The ceiling on medium- and long-term loans was also cut, to 1.35 percent from 1.55 percent.
A central bank official said the decision to ease monetary policy was taken because the persistent decline in consumer prices had left real interest rates too high.
The annual rate of inflation dropped to 2.9 percent this month, its lowest level since the communist country launched economic reforms in the late 1980s.
The offical added that the bank had also cut rates to tackle flagging demand for credit and encourage economic growth. The government expects GDP growth of nine to 10 percent this year.
Fearing an economic slowdown, the authorities have recently expressed concern about deflationary pressures.

Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong said last month that measures may be taken before year-end to prevent a slide in prices. The State Bank has said interest rates will be cut and the local currency, the dong, devalued.

Economists say they expect consumer prices to edge higher in coming months. The official Vietnam News Agency said on Tuesday that the government saw the annual inflation rate ending the year at six to seven percent.
